react_result.final_narrative_text: The ten-metabolite differential signature is almost entirely composed of C19/C18 steroid intermediates and products, producing an overwhelming cross-paradigm enrichment of the androgen and estrogen metabolism axis. RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-direct analysis all converge on KEGG:hsa00140 / map00150 as the top-ranked pathway (FDR 6.05e-18, p 5.77e-07 across methods). RaMP additionally identifies the Reactome steroid-hormone metabolism module (REACT:R-HSA-196071, FDR 5.33e-17) and WikiPathways steroid-biosynthesis (WP:WP496) and sulfatase-aromatase (WP:WP5368) pathways as significant, each with 5–6 input steroids as documented members. Mummichog's empirical-compound network independently recovers the same biology through mass-based seeding, ranking C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism first (p=0.000252) and androgen/estrogen biosynthesis second (p=0.000504), with 14–15 overlapping steroids. The six driver steroids — dehydroepiandrosterone (C01227), testosterone (C00535), androstenedione (C00280), estrone (C00468), 17β-estradiol (C00951), and dihydrotestosterone (C03917) — are all confirmed members of the KEGG:hsa00140 pathway roster. The four non-steroid metabolites (xanthine, beta-mercaptoethanol, coumarin, N-acetylgalactosamine) are absent from all steroid pathway member lists, confirming the signal is specific to steroidogenesis rather than global metabolic disturbance. The biological story is one of concerted steroid-hormone pathway perturbation: DHEA feeds both the androgen arm (testosterone → DHT) and the aromatase-conversion arm (androstenedione → estrone → estradiol), and six concurrent elevation of these C19/C18 steroids indicates a treatment-induced shift in the steroidogenic flux that spans both androgen and estrogen branches.

{
  "narrative_text": "The ten-metabolite differential signature is enriched for C19/C18 steroid intermediates and products across three independent analysis paradigms.
